heading: ## Abstract
context: We develop a finite Wonsik Reality–Renderer Architecture (WRRA) toy model to explore possible explanatory connections among quantum states and gravity, vacuum energy and expansion, and dark-matter and dark-energy effects. The purpose is model development and assessment of specified computational connections, rather than a claim to have solved these three problems or established WRRA as the physical theory of the universe. The guiding hypothesis is that one nonprivileged universe can be described through minimal computation, a common carrier and phenotype. The implemented model maps a finite SOURCE and conditional carrier states through sector admission to information loads, calibrated energy, pressure and downstream gravity and expansion responses. Verified constants and observed sector shares are disclosed construction inputs. We identify what follows from those inputs and the WRRA transformations, what is reproduced, and where the proposed connections remain incomplete. In a model with 1,014,999 active addresses and a 128-dimensional carrier, exact correlation-preserving reduction reproduces loads to 8.9×10⁻¹⁶. Identical separate marginals need not preserve joint loads or calculated deceleration. A class-resolved lift repairs a concrete controlled-update failure. Applying the frozen WRRA acceleration scale with the constitutive coefficient kappa=1/8 through the credited empirical RAR kernel to 2,693 published SPARC points gives 0.13288 dex RMS without a new fit. These results substantiate the toy model's interface, identify its dynamical and observational limits, and document descriptive consistency. They do not derive microscopic quantum gravity or the small cosmological constant. The contribution is an executable, auditable model of a shared explanatory chain, including a precise account of which microscopic distinctions its present macroscopic outputs cannot resolve.
